aliasConflicts.kimi: local canonical Moonshot platform API-key provider (open-sse/providers/registry/kimi.js, api.moonshot.ai); it is not a Kimi Coding device credential and must not be remapped
aliasConflicts.kimi-web: local Kimi consumer web session (open-sse/providers/registry/kimi-web.js, www.kimi.com / www.kimi.ai); its access/refresh pair is a browser session, not an OAuth device grant
aliasConflicts.kimi-coding-apikey: local Kimi Code API key (open-sse/providers/registry/kimi-coding-apikey.js); it authenticates with a static key and never runs the device flow

repository.name: EasyCLIProxyAPI
repository.note: desktop console around a separately versioned CLIProxyAPI core; it owns the Kimi Code CLI launch configuration (config.toml with base_url and api_key) and delegates every Kimi sign-in contract to that core, so it contributes no independent Kimi OAuth wire contract

exports.index.js: public staging exports (config.js and identity.js); no side effects on import

stagedDelta.summary: Kimi Coding requests and refreshes always present a stable, UUID-shaped device identity, and carry the device name and OS version headers both upstreams send.
productionNow: open-sse/config/appConstants.js buildKimiDeviceHeaders sends X-Msh-Platform, X-Msh-Version, X-Msh-Device-Model and X-Msh-Device-Id only; X-Msh-Device-Name and X-Msh-Os-Version are missing

open-sse/services/tokenRefresh/providers.js refreshKimiToken falls back to buildKimiHeaders() when a connection has no stored device id, which sends X-Msh-Device-Id: kimi-<timestamp> — a new identity on every refresh
open-sse/executors/default.js HEADER_HOOKS.kimiHeaders falls back to the same buildKimiHeaders() when no device id is stored
upstreamNow: CLIProxyAPI internal/auth/kimi/kimi.go commonHeaders sends platform, version, device name, device model and device id on the device, poll and refresh requests
OmniRoute open-sse/config/providers/registry/kimi/coding/runtime.ts buildKimiCodeIdentityHeaders sends the same five plus X-Msh-Os-Version
OmniRoute open-sse/services/tokenRefresh/providers/kimiCoding.ts derives a deterministic device id from the refresh token when no device id was stored

integration.sharedOAuth: src/lib/oauth/providers.js kimiDeviceProvider.requestDeviceCode and .pollToken — replace buildKimiDeviceHeaders(deviceId) with buildKimiDeviceIdentityHeaders({ platform, version, deviceId: resolveKimiDeviceId({ deviceId }) }) and keep the flow-owned device id in extraData._deviceId
integration.headerConfig: open-sse/config/appConstants.js buildKimiHeaders and buildKimiDeviceHeaders — add X-Msh-Device-Name and X-Msh-Os-Version; keep the legacy X-Msh-Platform: 9router value for the shared 9router-shaped callers and the DurinDoor value for the device flow
integration.refresh: open-sse/services/tokenRefresh/providers.js refreshKimiToken — replace the buildKimiHeaders() fallback with resolveKimiDeviceId({ deviceId: providerSpecificData?.deviceId, refreshToken }) so a legacy connection keeps one device across rotations
integration.requestHooks: open-sse/executors/default.js HEADER_HOOKS.kimiHeaders and HEADER_HOOKS.kimiDeviceHeaders — build the identity headers from the stored device id, falling back to the stored refresh token
integration.registry: open-sse/providers/registry/kimi-coding.js and open-sse/providers/registry/kimi-ai.js — the client id, device code URL, token URL and refresh URL rows already match the pinned upstream; no change queued
integration.batch: the shared OAuth wiring above belongs to the ordered auth batches, not to this unit; this unit only stages the helper and its contracts

restrictions: registered: false — the helper is not wired into production; the parity test keeps its staging assertions in one isolated block

Kimi Coding device credentials, the Moonshot platform API key, the Kimi Code API key and the Kimi consumer web session are four separate identities and must never share a token, a device id or a refresh path
the Kimi consumer web session refreshes through its own RPC endpoint; the OmniRoute web refresh path is not adopted here
synthetic tokens only; no live account, browser, Docker or provider traffic
no new auth gateway, framework or credential store; the existing OAuth provider object, connection model, flow store and storage are reused
